articles.title: Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair
articles.summary: The appointment was made after it emerged Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman believed to be a spy for China.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair
articles.summaryTr: The appointment was made after it emerged Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman believed to be a spy for China.
articles.articleText: Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair - Published Nvidia has hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate the affair between its chief executive and an alleged Chinese spy. Jensen Huang, a co-founder of Nvidia who has led it to become one of the most valuable companies in the world, admitted to having a romantic relationship with a woman outside of his marriage. The woman, Alice Huang, is alleged to be a spy for Beijing. She was an executive at a Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has been a customer of Nvidia. Nvidia said on Tuesday that Wachtell attorney Joon Kim was set to lead "a thorough and independent investigation" into Jensen Huang's affair. The FBI is also conducting its own probe. Nvidia is widely considered one of the most important companies behind the US artificial intelligence (AI) boom given it is the sole manufacturer of a crucial computer chip required for successfully operating AI tools. Shares in the company fell to a near-yearly low on Tuesday, wiping more than $500bn (£375bn) off Nvidia's stock market value since Friday, even as tech stocks have recovered since last week's sell-off. Jensen Huang's relationship with an executive of an Nvidia customer, who is also believed by the US government to be spying for China, has business and national security implications. Megaspeed had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia has said was investigated and debunked. Nvidia has also maintained the US government did not inform the firm that Megaspeed posed an intelligence concern. According to the New York Times, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington in spring of this year warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy. Beijing has rejected claims that Jensen Huang has been targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "intended to smear and malign China". US President Donald Trump said Monday that he had spoken to Jensen Huang and that the Nvidia boss told him "I had no idea she was a spy." Trump said he believed the him. However, the relationship has drawn more political attention. Congressional leaders of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs have asked Jensen Huang to appear next week for a closed door briefing. The Nvidia boss has yet to say whether he will attend, a person familiar with the committee's demand told the BBC. The committee has the authority to subpoena Jensen Huang, effectively forcing him to appear before the committee, if deemed necessary. When announcing on Sunday that it would investigate the affair, Nvidia's board said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised. It added that a committee of independent directors would oversee the probe. - What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy - Published40 minutes ago Joon Kim, who will lead Nvidia's investigation, is a former US Attorney for New York's Southern District and spent several years working as a government attorney focused on fraud and other criminal acts. Wachtell is one of the largest law firms in the US and has several notable clients in the tech industry. Among them are OpenAI and Salesforce. The investigation will likely be treated as urgent, according to sources familiar with the matter, as Jensen Huang's public image is tightly intertwined with Nvidia. He has become a key public figure in the development on AI, arguing the technology is a "new industrial revolution" and is on par with the advent of electricity. It is unclear, however, if Wachtell will be able to interview Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, and is not related to Jensen Huang. A spokesperson for Nvidia declined to comment on Tuesday when asked if Jensen Huang had retained any additional of his own legal representation amid the company investigation and the separate one launched by the FBI. - Published13 hours ago

articles.title: Can crypto trust firms compete with banks in US derivatives settlements?
articles.summary: Crypto custodians are moving into a market handling billions in daily settlements, but regulatory relief and a shift in congressional control leave questions over their long-term role.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Can crypto trust firms compete with banks in US derivatives settlements?
articles.summaryTr: Crypto custodians are moving into a market handling billions in daily settlements, but regulatory relief and a shift in congressional control leave questions over their long-term role.
articles.articleText: Can crypto trust firms compete with banks in US derivatives settlements? Crypto custodians are moving into a market handling billions in daily settlements, but regulatory relief and a shift in congressional control leave questions over their long-term role. Crypto companies are moving deeper into financial services traditionally dominated by banks, seeking a role in US derivatives settlements, where billions of dollars change hands daily. The push comes as regulators expand the services trust companies can provide, even as traditional banking groups challenge parts of the regulatory framework governing crypto firms’ expansion into banklike activities. A Nov. 5 decision by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) illustrates the shift, allowing derivatives clearinghouses to use trust companies for daily settlements with clearing members, a function previously restricted to banks under the agency’s regulations. The relief could create new business opportunities for regulated crypto custodians, but its revocable nature and changes in the US political landscape raise questions about the durability of the regulatory opening. Crypto firms eye billions in daily derivatives settlements The scale of the derivatives settlement business offers some perspective on the opportunity. CME Group, one of the world’s largest derivatives market operators, transferred an average of $8.7 billion per business day through its clearing systems during the first half of 2026, up from $6.7 billion a day in 2025, according to regulatory filings. Those figures represent funds transferred between clearing firms to settle gains and losses, rather than fees earned by settlement banks. They nevertheless illustrate the scale of financial flows supported by the infrastructure that trust companies could increasingly help provide. The CFTC’s Division of Clearing and Risk issued no-action relief on Nov. 5 following an Oct. 29 request from derivatives clearinghouse Nodal Clear, allowing clearinghouses to use trust companies for daily settlements if they meet the same evaluation and monitoring requirements applied to traditional settlement banks. The decision addresses an inconsistency between federal commodities law, which permits customer funds to be held at banks or trust companies, and CFTC Regulation 39.14, which defines settlement banks only as banks. Nodal Clear partnered with Coinbase in 2025 to integrate USDC into US futures trading. Coinbase Custody Trust was already expected to provide daily settlement services under the arrangement, Cointelegraph has learned. Related: CFTC expands regulatory relief for passive trading software providers Other crypto firms have also expanded their institutional financial services. On Nov. 4, BitGo launched its Global Markets division, combining derivatives trading, financing, collateral management and settlement capabilities. Coinbase’s national trust bank charter also took effect on Nov. 6, allowing Coinbase National Trust Company, a separate entity from Coinbase Custody Trust, to provide federally supervised digital asset custody services. Several major crypto firms have also secured US national trust bank approvals over the past months, including Circle, Ripple, Crypto.com and Stripe-owned Bridge. The charters, granted by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), reflect the industry’s expansion into federally regulated financial services. Traditional banks contest crypto firms’ expanding role The expansion of specialized trust companies has prompted objections from traditional banking groups. In October, the Independent Community Bankers of America sued the OCC, arguing that its national trust bank charter rules could allow crypto firms to conduct certain banklike activities without meeting all the requirements imposed on conventional banks. The lawsuit reflects a broader disagreement over how specialized financial institutions should be regulated as they expand into services also provided by banks. Cody Carbone, CEO of The Digital Chamber, told Cointelegraph that the CFTC’s relief does not put trust companies in a better or worse position than traditional banks. Trust companies and banks already compete for services permitted under their respective charters, Carbone said, adding that the decision gives clearinghouses more options without preventing banks from retaining their business. “A trust company charter is not a regulatory shortcut,” he said. Revocable relief faces a changing regulatory landscape Despite the potential opportunities, the CFTC’s decision leaves questions about how securely trust companies can establish a long-term role in derivatives settlement. The agency issued a no-action letter rather than formally amending its regulations. The letter states that CFTC staff will not recommend enforcement action against clearinghouses using trust companies for daily settlements if specified conditions are met. Unlike a formal rule amendment, which generally requires a public notice-and-comment process, staff no-action relief does not change the underlying regulation and can be withdrawn. “A change in Commission leadership could withdraw the CFTC Letter. More formal Commission action, such as amending the regulation, would be necessary to avoid this potential risk,” Jordan Yeagley, a shareholder at Buchanan Ingersoll & Rooney, told Cointelegraph. The uncertainty comes at a politically significant moment for the agency. CFTC Chair Michael Selig remains the regulator’s sole commissioner, despite a statutory structure providing for five commissioners. Selig has led the agency since December 2025, leaving four seats vacant as the regulator expands its work on digital asset markets. The political environment is also changing following the Nov. 3 US midterm elections, in which Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress. The incoming Congress, which takes office in January, will have greater power to scrutinize the CFTC’s regulatory agenda. The Senate also has a role in confirming nominees to fill the agency’s vacant commissioner seats, while the House and Senate Agriculture Committees oversee the regulator. Sen. Sherrod Brown, who won Ohio’s Senate race on Nov. 3 despite more than $60 million in opposition spending from crypto-backed political action committees, could take on a prominent role on the Senate Agriculture Committee. articles.titleTr: Across Protocol warns users to avoid app amid reports of drained wallets
articles.summaryTr: The protocol is investigating a potential security incident affecting its domain, while several users have reported losing funds after interacting with the platform.
articles.articleText: Across Protocol warns users to avoid app amid reports of drained wallets The protocol is investigating a potential security incident affecting its domain, while several users have reported losing funds after interacting with the platform. Crosschain bridging protocol Across, which allows users to transfer digital assets between Ethereum and other blockchain networks, warned users Tuesday not to access its app or connect their wallets while it investigates a potential security incident. In a Tuesday X post, Across advised users against signing transactions or approvals until further notice, without specifying the nature of the incident or whether its website had been compromised. Source: Across Protocol On X, one user claimed to have lost $9,000 in USDC, while another reported losing 7,053 USDT0 across seven transactions on the Plasma blockchain. A third user said their wallet was drained after using the bridge several times, alleging that the website had been compromised. Across asked the users for transaction details to investigate their reports. Cointelegraph has not independently verified the reports. Across Protocol did not immediately respond to Cointelegraph’s request for more details. Across Protocol responds to user reporting $9,000 USDC loss. Source: X user bilm01 NEAR AI discloses separate security breach In a separate security incident, NEAR AI disclosed Monday that attackers exploited a vulnerability in its AI infrastructure, exposing account details belonging to approximately 100 users and data from 18 AI agents. According to a Nov. 9 incident report, attackers exploited a remote code execution vulnerability in SGLang, an open-source AI inference engine, to gain access to an internal server and other infrastructure. The compromised data included user names, email addresses, agent chat histories, settings and logs, while two customers had API keys exposed. NEAR AI said attackers may also have observed requests processed on the compromised server, including those running in confidential mode. The company said it had patched the vulnerability, revoked exposed credentials and restored access to its cloud services. articles.summary: A majority of 49 to 24 assembly members backed the legislation, which was proposed by Sinn Féin's Danny Baker and welcomed by some parents and charities.

articles.titleTr: Law on 'holiday hunger' passed by Stormont assembly
articles.summaryTr: A majority of 49 to 24 assembly members backed the legislation, which was proposed by Sinn Féin's Danny Baker and welcomed by some parents and charities.
articles.articleText: Law on 'holiday hunger' passed by Stormont assembly - Published A law aimed at helping lower income families with food costs during school holidays has been passed by the Northern Ireland Assembly. The Holiday Meal Payments Bill seeks to create a new payment for families whose children receive free school meals to help with food costs outside of term time. A majority of 49 to 24 assembly members backed the legislation, which was proposed by Sinn Féin's Danny Baker and welcomed by some parents and charities. Education Minister Paul Givan described the bill as "fiscally reckless", warning it would cost £20m to £30m a year and lead to cuts elsewhere within his Stormont department. Baker said that "poverty isn't green and orange" and the passage of the bill would support thousands of children "across all of our communities". "When children are returning to school hungry, then they're not learning," he told assembly members during the bill's final stage debate. "If you want to deal with educational underachievement then you have to deal with poverty." Givan described the bill as "well intentioned" but said "sincerity is not a funding model". The Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) minister added there was "no such thing as a free lunch" and the legislation "will require cuts to be made" to other services. "So I ask those who support this bill, what cuts should be made to afford this payment?" The minister argued efforts at Stormont to tackle poverty should be made "in a coordinated way" across the entire four-party executive. Last month, Givan's department tabled amendments that would have given him power to delay its implementation, but these were rejected by a majority of parties. Funding for bill 'relatively small' Stormont assembly members voted on the bill on Tuesday night after more than four hours of debate during its final stage in the chamber. Alliance Party assembly member Nick Mathison, chair of the assembly's education committee, said "holiday hunger" remained a significant issue for many families. He acknowledged Stormont's financial pressures but said the funding required for the bill was a "relatively small" proportion of the Department of Education's budget. "When we are in a budgetary crisis we need to be ensuring that we do not end up penalising those who are least able to bear the costs," he added. Ulster Unionist Party (UUP) leader Jon Burrows commended Baker on the sentiment of his private member's bill but warned "there is no funding stream and there is no money". He said the bill "lacks any governance", adding: "There are no guarantees the money given under this will end up in nutritious meals inside the stomachs of children." "It's a fundamental misapplication and misunderstanding of how the welfare system should work," he told assembly members. Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP) assembly member Cara Hunter welcomed the bill, saying that "a child can't learn on an empty stomach". "Hunger shows up in concentration, in behaviour and attainment long before it shows up in the spreadsheets or the speeches that we have before us here today," she added. Why was the bill introduced? Baker said he was motivated to introduce it by some of his experiences of breakfast clubs and meal schemes in youth work. "There was a young boy, about the same age of my youngest, around seven years old," he explained. "He was filling his wee pockets up and we caught on to this. "To cut a long story short, he was bringing home food for his siblings because there just wasn't enough food in the house." Baker said all ministers had choices to make and the legislation alone could not solve child poverty, but would act as an "early intervention". Children are eligible for free school meals if their family's household income is below £15,390 a year. Northern Ireland is the only UK region without government-funded holiday food support, after the Department of Education (DE) ended its £27-per-fortnight holiday meal grant in 2023. Baker's legislation was introduced in the Northern Ireland Assembly in March and has been scrutinised by members of the legislative assembly (MLAs) on a number of occasions over the past nine months. What have campaigners and charities said? Community and voluntary groups have been publicly supportive of the bill, with some staging a demonstration at Stormont on Monday in a bid to urge MLAs to get it over the finish line. Louise McCullough, a mum-of-three from east Belfast, was among those who spoke at the event. She said her children receive free school meals and that she would be directly affected by the legislation. "There are so many working families who need this, it will change their lives and be massively impactful," she told BBC News NI. "I can't afford to work full time because of the cost of childcare, and the cost of living. "We have to do what we can and schemes like free school meals make a difference but so much more needs done... if you can't find money for hungry children what are you doing? "Our government should be scaffolding our families properly." Edel Diamond from the South West Belfast Foodbank said organisations like hers had been "filling in the gaps" to help struggling families. "We shouldn't have to - it's incumbent on our executive to put these initiatives forward," she said. "This will make such a difference to families we're seeing daily." - Published30 March 2023 - Published12 October

articles.summary: The 82-year-old was placed under house detention in Florida last week after being charged over possession of child sex abuse material.

articles.titleTr: Meghan's father Thomas Markle detained for allegedly cutting off ankle monitor, officials say
articles.summaryTr: The 82-year-old was placed under house detention in Florida last week after being charged over possession of child sex abuse material.
articles.articleText: Meghan's father Thomas Markle detained for allegedly cutting off ankle monitor, officials say - Published Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, has been detained in Florida for allegedly removing his ankle monitor, according to justice department officials in Los Angeles. Markle appeared before a federal magistrate judge in the Florida city of Tampa after allegedly removing the monitor at 01:45 local time (06:45 GMT), a justice department (DoJ) spokesperson told the BBC. The judge ordered him jailed without bond and he is now in federal custody, the spokesperson said. Markle, who has previously denied possessing images of child sex abuse, was arrested in Florida last week and placed under house detention. He was also ordered to wear a location monitoring device. The BBC has contacted his representatives. US Judge Lindsay S Griffin said on Tuesday that Markle's housing situation "had become untenable", according to court documents. Griffin cited a "lack of suitable housing", writing in the order that "no condition or combination of conditions would reasonably assure the safety of any other person or the community and the defendant's appearance in court". He also ordered a medical evaluation for Markle and said he "must receive all necessary and prescribed medication unless discontinued by a physician". "Release conditions are court orders, not suggestions," Bill Essayli, the US attorney for Central California, wrote on X on Tuesday about Markle's alleged removal of his ankle monitor. "We will continue to prosecute this case to the fullest extent of the law," Essayli added. Markle was first arrested last week after the FBI, acting on warrants, searched storage units in Los Angeles registered to him which he had rented since 2008, with the last payment being made in October this year, the DoJ said. Inside the units the FBI says agents seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books that they allege contained child sex abuse material. Witnesses "positively identified" Markle in two of the images believed to contain child sex abuse material. In those images, the man pictured "appears to be in the age range of 30s to 40s", which suggests the alleged abuse dates back decades as Markle is currently 82 years old. Markle appeared in court last week following his arrest. No plea was taken during the appearance, which set several conditions for his pretrial release, including that he be kept in home detention. He is charged with one count of possessing indecent images of children, according to the DoJ. FBI director Kash Patel said last week that Markle "allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions". Markle has called the allegations "sick lies". He moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes, and lived in Cebu until May. He was reportedly learning to walk again in Florida after having his leg amputated. The duchess has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls. In a previously shared statement, Meghan confirmed the existence of the letter and wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed." She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children". articles.title: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
articles.summary: The billionaire tech executive finds himself mired in a personal and national security scandal.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
articles.summaryTr: The billionaire tech executive finds himself mired in a personal and national security scandal.
articles.articleText: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy - Published One of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) industry's most important figures has been accused of having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. US intelligence officials believed that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Nvidia CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report. Jensen Huang admitted, external to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. US tech giant Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, has opened an independent investigation into the affair. It said it does not believe US national security had been compromised - and added that Jensen Huang was committed to continuing to lead the company. Here is what we know about the affair and why it matters. Who is Alice Huang and what do we know about the affair? US officials believed that Alice Huang had been recruited to spy by China's top intelligence agency, the New York Times reported, external. Her current whereabouts are unknown. Alice Huang, who is of no relation to Jensen Huang, was a top executive at Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed between March and November 2023. The firm had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia maintains was investigated and debunked. However, Megaspeed is under investigation by the Singapore government regarding previous allegations that the company was circumventing US sanctions on the export of Nvidia's high-end chips. The BBC has contacted Megaspeed for comment. The company told the New York Times last month its current leadership took the allegations seriously and had appointed external legal advisers to conduct an internal investigation. Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang through a process known as "unmasking". It remains unclear what, if any, intelligence Alice Huang – who is also known as Huang Le – allegedly gathered and passed to Beijing. She did not respond to the paper's request for comment. When the BBC asked Nvidia if the company was aware of intelligence concerns, the company said it was not. "We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the US government would have notified us," an Nvidia spokesperson told the BBC. China has rejected the spying allegations. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters: "The allegations about Chinese spies are entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China." The New York Times reported in late October that US President Donald Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence alleging Alice Huang was spying on China's behalf. Asked by reporters on Sunday whether he wished he had "acted on the intelligence", Trump responded: "No, I don't think so. I think he's [Jensen Huang] an honourable guy." US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, meanwhile, refused to comment when asked about Jensen Huang. Last spring, the secretary of state reportedly oversaw the drafting of a memo that warned the Trump administration about Jensen Huang's relationship with the Chinese businesswoman. - Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy - Published13 hours ago - Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair - Published3 minutes ago Why does it matter? Nvidia is at the heart of US and China's AI race, which is why the billionaire's affair has sparked national security fears among American lawmakers. Trump has said "whoever wins AI wins", and the fear is that if China gains the upper hand in AI, it will supercharge the country's military and surveillance capabilities. The US advantage is in large part because of US companies like Nvidia, working with producers like the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), which makes more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips. Since 2022, the US has used various export controls to keep the top tech out of China, which it says helps retain America's competitive edge and protects its national security. This means companies like Nvidia have been largely locked out of the world's most lucrative market, with Jensen Huang once saying that Nvidia's share of the Chinese market had gone from around 95% to effectively zero. Huang has engaged in shuttle diplomacy between Washington and Beijing, hoping to find a US-approved way back in, and shaping US policy on China along the way. Sunday's revelations may explain why Jensen Huang has failed to bring home the biggest prize of all to Nvidia: the Trump administration's blessing to sell all but its most advanced chips to China. Who is Jensen Huang? Born in Taiwan in 1963, Jensen Huang was nine years old when his family moved to the West Coast of the US. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University. Jensen Huang then worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia. Known as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan and once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech", he has a reputation as a workaholic and perfectionist with incredibly high standards for his staff. He has an estimated fortune of $155bn (£115bn), according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. "Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine, a biography on the Jensen Huang, told the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today. The Nvidia co-founder has a famously close relationship with Trump. At the recent AI summit at the White House, where 42 tech executives were present, the president was flanked by Elon Musk and Jensen Huang. Trump said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him "'Did you have any idea she was a spy?'" "He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters. What investigations are now under way? Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into the affair and has hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to carry out the probe. The investigation will be led by former US Attorney for New York's Southern District, Joon Kim. US President Donald Trump said on Monday that the FBI was also investigating the affair. The FBI declined to comment further when contacted by the BBC. Jensen Huang has also been asked to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees on 18 November. Members of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee asked the Nvidia chief executive to appear to explain his interactions with Alice Huang, as well as Nvidia's security protocols around espionage. Jensen Huang has yet to say he will comply, a person familiar with the committee's demand told the BBC. What is Nvidia and how important is it? Founded by Jensen Huang and fellow electrical engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem in 1993, the company was originally known for chips that process graphics, particularly for computer games. Eventually it changed focus to AI, a field it now dominates. Jensen Huang rescued Nvidia from bankruptcy on more than one occasion, and took risks on AI a long time before the rest of the world did, effectively building the infrastructure from scratch. "Today when we think of that, we think of these giant data centres - none of that existed. There were no customers for the stuff he was building. In fact his first customer was Open AI at the time they had 30 people - he actually gave it to them, he donated it to them," Witt told the BBC. Every notable tech company building AI tools and infrastructure, including Amazon, Meta, Google, and Microsoft, now use Nvidia chips. Currently worth about $4tn, Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies in the world. For now, the firm's board appears to have little appetite for removing Jensen Huang, saying in a statement on Sunday that they have "confidence in Jensen and his leadership team". Sources tell the BBC his removal is unlikely because there is so much money at stake. There is no public succession plan for the 63-year-old. He has often said he hopes to continue in the role for decades, and Bloomberg reports he has created an informal leadership structure around him unlike a traditional company's hierarchy. articles.articleTextTr: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy - Published One of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) industry's most important figures has been accused of having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. US intelligence officials believed that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Nvidia CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report. Jensen Huang admitted, external to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. US tech giant Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, has opened an independent investigation into the affair. It said it does not believe US national security had been compromised - and added that Jensen Huang was committed to continuing to lead the company. Here is what we know about the affair and why it matters. Who is Alice Huang and what do we know about the affair? US officials believed that Alice Huang had been recruited to spy by China's top intelligence agency, the New York Times reported, external. Her current whereabouts are unknown. Alice Huang, who is of no relation to Jensen Huang, was a top executive at Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed between March and November 2023. The firm had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia maintains was investigated and debunked. However, Megaspeed is under investigation by the Singapore government regarding previous allegations that the company was circumventing US sanctions on the export of Nvidia's high-end chips. The BBC has contacted Megaspeed for comment. The company told the New York Times last month its current leadership took the allegations seriously and had appointed external legal advisers to conduct an internal investigation. Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang through a process known as "unmasking". It remains unclear what, if any, intelligence Alice Huang – who is also known as Huang Le – allegedly gathered and passed to Beijing. She did not respond to the paper's request for comment. When the BBC asked Nvidia if the company was aware of intelligence concerns, the company said it was not. "We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the US government would have notified us," an Nvidia spokesperson told the BBC. China has rejected the spying allegations. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters: "The allegations about Chinese spies are entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China." US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, meanwhile, refused to comment when asked about Jensen Huang. Nvidia is at the heart of US and China's AI race, which is why the billionaire's affair has sparked national security fears among American lawmakers. Trump has said "whoever wins AI wins", and the fear is that if China gains the upper hand in AI, it will supercharge the country's military and surveillance capabilities. The US advantage is in large part because of US companies like Nvidia, working with producers like the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), which makes more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips. Since 2022, the US has used various export controls to keep the top tech out of China, which it says helps retain America's competitive edge and protects its national security. This means companies like Nvidia have been largely locked out of the world's most lucrative market, with Jensen Huang once saying that Nvidia's share of the Chinese market had gone from around 95% to effectively zero. Huang has engaged in shuttle diplomacy between Washington and Beijing, hoping to find a US-approved way back in, and shaping US policy on China along the way. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University. Jensen Huang then worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia. Known as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan and once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech", he has a reputation as a workaholic and perfectionist with incredibly high standards for his staff. He has an estimated fortune of $155bn (£115bn), according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. "Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine, a biography on the Jensen Huang, told the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today. At the recent AI summit at the White House, where 42 tech executives were present, the president was flanked by Elon Musk and Jensen Huang. Trump said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him "'Did you have any idea she was a spy?'" "He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters. Founded by Jensen Huang and fellow electrical engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem in 1993, the company was originally known for chips that process graphics, particularly for computer games. articles.titleTr: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says
articles.summaryTr: Delegations from Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are in the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
articles.articleText: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says - Published The first of two days of trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine has concluded in Abu Dhabi. While senior officials from Kyiv and Moscow were tight-lipped after the four hour-long discussions, President Volodymyr Zelensky, who was not at the talks, said they had proved "constructive and quite substantive". Speaking from Paris, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also said the meeting had been "very productive". Although expectations for a breakthrough that ends Russia's full-scale war on Ukraine are low, US officials said earlier that Moscow and Kyiv were privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would control Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario. Zelensky also said that humanitarian issues such as prisoner of war exchanges had been discussed. At the start of Tuesday's talks President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, told delegates that the US had "narrowed the gaps" between the two sides, without providing details, and hoped to move towards a "solution that hopefully ends the war". Kushner had said earlier the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine. Asked later at a news conference in Copenhagen about the approach of US officials to negotiations, Zelensky said: "I see changes. I'm very happy with what I hear." Kushner and Trump peace envoy Steve Witkoff also met Ukrainian and European and Nato officials on the sidelines of the main meeting. Until now European leaders have largely been excluded from peace talks, but they have pushed to be included in the discussions amid concerns that decisions about their continent's security would be made without them. The Americans appear to support this, with Rubio acknowledging during a visit to Paris that the Europeans "are a part of solving this problem for the long term". However, "the Russians have a bad taste in their mouth with the Europeans", according to a US official. Some proposals favoured by EU officials - such as calling an unconditional ceasefire as a prerequisite for peace negotiations - are routinely rejected by Moscow. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said on Tuesday that a truce would just allow Kyiv to regroup. "We will not agree to it," he said. Moscow and Kyiv's positions are still far apart on ending the conflict. A key area of disagreement involves Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is mostly occupied by Russia. Moscow has demanded that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk it still holds, while Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those areas, which it says are crucial to its future security. While neither side has budged on these demands, the US official speaking on the eve of the talks suggested that this was just the public stance and that Moscow and Kyiv had shown "a little bit of flexibility, privately". However, he acknowledged the issue would not be solved without discussions about a new "security architecture". "They will not solve the Donetsk issue and the territorial issue until they know what the security architecture is going to be after the war," the official said. "And keep in mind, we're not going to be able to finalise one without the other." For Ukraine, a post-war "security architecture" may include reassurance that allies will come to its aid if it comes under attack again. For Russia, that could be its longstanding ambition to see Nato roll back from Eastern Europe – which would be alarming to Europeans. The framework being proposed includes security consultations and crisis communications hotlines, as well as "reciprocal de-escalation measures" between the two. The officials also floated the re-activation of the Nato-Russia Council that has been largely paused since 2022. The last round of trilateral talks, held in Geneva in February, ended without a breakthrough. Soon after, the US-Israel war on Iran diverted Washington's attention from Ukraine, and no other discussions were held since. From the start of his second term in office, US President Donald Trump – who once boasted he could end the war in Ukraine within a day – has spearheaded several rounds of talks to end the conflict, albeit with little success. Meanwhile, his increasingly conciliatory approach towards Moscow has fuelled deep unease in Kyiv and across the European Union. After meeting Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Washington last week, Trump touted a forthcoming "big, beautiful agreement" on Ukraine that "might involve all of Europe". Many in Ukraine are sceptical that this would result in a fair peace. Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko, head of the foreign affairs parliamentary committee, told the BBC he believed Trump wanted "a quick deal at the expense of Ukraine", which will certainly be rejected by Kyiv. The only way to make Russia's Vladimir Putin start real negotiations was by putting greater pressure on Russia through sanctions and deep strikes, Merezhko said. "While Putin has a war machine up and running, he has no incentives to negotiate." He also mentioned recent moves by Trump, such as his deal to buy diesel from Russia, as something that "only encourages Moscow to continue the war". Moscow's delegation in Abu Dhabi includes Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky, deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, spy chief Igor Kostyukov and army general Yury Zhigarlovsky. Kyiv has sent several senior officials who have been part of previous negotiating teams, including Foreign Intelligence Service head Rustem Umerov, Volodymyr Zelensky's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, and MP Davyd Arakhamiya. Away from Abu Dhabi, Russia continues to pummel Ukraine with deadly bombardments and strikes on energy infrastructure, viewed in Kyiv as proof that Moscow wants to corner Ukraine into accepting a deal on Russia's terms. On Monday, Kushner was cautious to point out that the Abu Dhabi talks could at most "build momentum toward the next phase of negotiations". "This is an extraordinarily difficult and complicated conflict," he wrote on X, adding the US was "approaching these discussions with determination and realism." articles.title: Why does Australia want Brits to swap Sydney for the outback?
articles.summary: Australia wants changes to UK deal that would push backpackers out of Bondi and into remote regions.

articles.titleTr: Why does Australia want Brits to swap Sydney for the outback?
articles.summaryTr: Australia wants changes to UK deal that would push backpackers out of Bondi and into remote regions.
articles.articleText: Why does Australia want Brits to swap Sydney for the outback? - Published In a Mexican restaurant in north-east Australia, the nacho bowls are served by staff from France, Italy, Ireland and Argentina. Cairns has long attracted a young and transient international crowd, who enjoy the tropical lifestyle while earning money for travel. But one nationality is in shorter supply than it used to be. "You get far fewer British backpackers looking for jobs here these days," says Mexicairns owner Peter McLeay. It's a trend McLeay has noticed since mid-2023, when a free trade deal between the UK and Australia kicked in. That agreement - as well as tariff-free trade in Tim Tams and Penguins - included special treatment for Brits on working holiday visas: exemption from having to find jobs in regional or remote places if they wanted to remain beyond a year. That, along with an increase in the age limit from 30 to 35 saw backpacker visas issued to Brits surging from 47,200 in 2023-24 to just over 77,000 in 2025-26, according to the latest Australian government data. Without the incentive to go regional, many are choosing to base themselves in the big cities, or, according to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, "Bondi or Coogee" - two of Sydney's most famous beachside suburbs. Now though, with Brits making up almost a quarter of all 323,000 backpacker visas issued last year, his government wants the free trade deal to be revisited. A privilege not enjoyed by others "Many Brits don't treat it as a working holiday anymore. It's more a three-year career break," says Dan McConnell, general manager of the Mad Monkey backpacker hostel chain. He says Brits used to be the largest clientele at its Cairns accommodation but "now French outnumber British three to one". "We see the Brits get to Sydney, decide it's the coolest place in the world, and stay there," he adds. It's a privilege not enjoyed by working holidaymakers from other countries who must do at least 88 days of "specified regional work" in industries that need a seasonal or temporary workforce - including agriculture, fisheries, tourism and hospitality - if they want to quality for a second year extension, and six months to stay a third year. Barely a month ago, Albanese ruled out forcing British backpackers to do the same, accepting it as part of the trade deal. But, under pressure from businesses here in Far North Queensland and other regional Australian communities, who are concerned about a lack of labour, the mood music has changed. Last week Albanese met UK counterpart Andy Burnham at the meeting of Commonwealth leaders in the Caribbean. And alongside AI, gender violence online and the AUKUS defence pact, backpackers were on the agenda. Despite speculation in the Australian media, no immediate announcement was made. Albanese instead told reporters that he had pushed for a change in the rules on backpackers and that Burnham had been "very constructive about it". "We'll work those issues through over coming weeks," he said adding that the free trade agreement was not set in stone and tweaks could be made "if there are good policy reasons". Backpackers make up one in seven farm jobs across Australia, with about 52,000 people on working holiday visas doing jobs in horticulture each year, according to the National Farmers Federation. It welcomed Albanese's discussions with Burnham, but said the issue of worker shortages in agriculture was far broader than the UK deal. Of greater concern are wider proposals, announced in September, to cut net migration into Australia, under political pressure from the resurgent right wing populist One Nation party and the opposition coalition. That includes an overhaul of the working holiday visa system, introducing a ballot for backpackers wanting to extend their stay – capped at 45,000 for people wanting a second year in Australia (down from 57,000 who qualified this year) and just 5,000 allowed to remain for a third year (compared with 31,000 this year). This, the federation says, is "a low blow". Those plans are still out for consultation, but immigration officials have slowed processing rates for some working holiday visa applications and paused them from several countries. Tourism Tropical North Queensland chief executive Mark Olsen has also been among those lobbying Albanese in Canberra - telling him that backpackers brought both the spending power and the temporary labour needed to fill seasonal roles in a region famed as a gateway to the Great Barrier Reef and the Unesco world heritage listed Daintree rainforest. Young Brits temporarily living and working in this region peaked at around 20,000 he says. Now it's closer to 11,000. "Numbers have dropped significantly since the UK free trade agreement kicked in when border arrangements returned to normal [after the pandemic] in 2023 ," he said. A two-way street Cairns restaurateur Fintan Rafferty says that of about 180 staff on his payroll across four venues, only five are British. Prior to the visa rule change, that was closer to 25. UK workers came with good skills in hospitality and "were willing to work, and to work flexible hours", he told the BBC. And, he said, it was a two-way street. "The pay is very good, the conditions are very good. And one of the great things about the 88-days rule is that it forces people to travel. It's enriching their experience." Bucking the trend, at the bar of Gilligan's backpackers, Paige Tomlinson serves vodka and soda with plenty of ice and a broad South Yorkshire accent. The 27-year-old, from Barnsley, has been in Cairns for four months, attracted by the "chilled" lifestyle and local waterfalls. "Most people prefer Sydney and they question me all the time why I'm here," she laughs. "But I got to Sydney and I just didn't like it. It was too busy, too much like London and I don't like London." She says she'd like to see the regional work requirement brought in for all Brits, "getting them out their comfort zone". "If every other country's got to do it, why should we not?" About 200km north, at Red Valley Farm in Lakeland, general manger Peter Inderbitzen agrees. Workers mainly from Tonga, hired on a Pacific labour scheme, pick bananas there year-round, But Inderbitzen also relies heavily on backpackers, especially at peak avocado season, employing about 25 people for a couple of months each year. "It's very short, sharp, get it done, get it out kind of work," he told the BBC. "But without those pickers, the avos stay on the tree." While a few British backpackers were still applying for work, numbers had "completely dropped off" since the rule change, said Inderbitzen, who'd "love" to see British travellers having an incentive to head to the regions. "As much as it wasn't perfect, [that programme] was working." Back in Cairns, most of the young Brits the BBC tracks down are on tourist visas - but many want to return for a working holiday. Among them is Ethan Phillips, 23, from Buckinghamshire who has been having way too much fun to keep up to date with what politicians have been discussing. "It makes sense for them to want us to do [regional work] again," he says. "I mean I'd rather not do it, but if we have to, it's only three months … it can't be that bad."

It's a privilege not enjoyed by working holidaymakers from other countries who must do at least 88 days of "specified regional work" in industries that need a seasonal or temporary workforce - including agriculture, fisheries, tourism and hospitality - if they want to quality for a second year extension, and six months to stay a third year. Barely a month ago, Albanese ruled out forcing British backpackers to do the same, accepting it as part of the trade deal. But, under pressure from businesses here in Far North Queensland and other regional Australian communities, who are concerned about a lack of labour, the mood music has changed. Last week Albanese met UK counterpart Andy Burnham at the meeting of Commonwealth leaders in the Caribbean. And alongside AI, gender violence online and the AUKUS defence pact, backpackers were on the agenda. Despite speculation in the Australian media, no immediate announcement was made. Albanese instead told reporters that he had pushed for a change in the rules on backpackers and that Burnham had been "very constructive about it". "We'll work those issues through over coming weeks," he said adding that the free trade agreement was not set in stone and tweaks could be made "if there are good policy reasons". Backpackers make up one in seven farm jobs across Australia, with about 52,000 people on working holiday visas doing jobs in horticulture each year, according to the National Farmers Federation. It welcomed Albanese's discussions with Burnham, but said the issue of worker shortages in agriculture was far broader than the UK deal. Of greater concern are wider proposals, announced in September, to cut net migration into Australia, under political pressure from the resurgent right wing populist One Nation party and the opposition coalition. That includes an overhaul of the working holiday visa system, introducing a ballot for backpackers wanting to extend their stay – capped at 45,000 for people wanting a second year in Australia (down from 57,000 who qualified this year) and just 5,000 allowed to remain for a third year (compared with 31,000 this year). This, the federation says, is "a low blow". Those plans are still out for consultation, but immigration officials have slowed processing rates for some working holiday visa applications and paused them from several countries. Tourism Tropical North Queensland chief executive Mark Olsen has also been among those lobbying Albanese in Canberra - telling him that backpackers brought both the spending power and the temporary labour needed to fill seasonal roles in a region famed as a gateway to the Great Barrier Reef and the Unesco world heritage listed Daintree rainforest. Young Brits temporarily living and working in this region peaked at around 20,000 he says. Now it's closer to 11,000. "Numbers have dropped significantly since the UK free trade agreement kicked in when border arrangements returned to normal [after the pandemic] in 2023 ," he said. A two-way street Cairns restaurateur Fintan Rafferty says that of about 180 staff on his payroll across four venues, only five are British. Prior to the visa rule change, that was closer to 25. UK workers came with good skills in hospitality and "were willing to work, and to work flexible hours", he told the BBC. And, he said, it was a two-way street. "The pay is very good, the conditions are very good. And one of the great things about the 88-days rule is that it forces people to travel. It's enriching their experience." Bucking the trend, at the bar of Gilligan's backpackers, Paige Tomlinson serves vodka and soda with plenty of ice and a broad South Yorkshire accent. The 27-year-old, from Barnsley, has been in Cairns for four months, attracted by the "chilled" lifestyle and local waterfalls. "Most people prefer Sydney and they question me all the time why I'm here," she laughs. "But I got to Sydney and I just didn't like it. It was too busy, too much like London and I don't like London." She says she'd like to see the regional work requirement brought in for all Brits, "getting them out their comfort zone". "If every other country's got to do it, why should we not?" About 200km north, at Red Valley Farm in Lakeland, general manger Peter Inderbitzen agrees. Workers mainly from Tonga, hired on a Pacific labour scheme, pick bananas there year-round, But Inderbitzen also relies heavily on backpackers, especially at peak avocado season, employing about 25 people for a couple of months each year. "It's very short, sharp, get it done, get it out kind of work," he told the BBC. "But without those pickers, the avos stay on the tree." While a few British backpackers were still applying for work, numbers had "completely dropped off" since the rule change, said Inderbitzen, who'd "love" to see British travellers having an incentive to head to the regions. "As much as it wasn't perfect, [that programme] was working." Back in Cairns, most of the young Brits the BBC tracks down are on tourist visas - but many want to return for a working holiday. Among them is Ethan Phillips, 23, from Buckinghamshire who has been having way too much fun to keep up to date with what politicians have been discussing. "It makes sense for them to want us to do [regional work] again," he says. "I mean I'd rather not do it, but if we have to, it's only three months … it can't be that bad."

articles.articleText: Resmi Gazete'de yayımlandı: Ozan Elektronik Para'nın faaliyet izni kaldırıldı YAYIN TARİHİ, 11 Kasım 2026 00:15 PAYLAŞ - TCMB, Ozan Elektronik Para AŞ'nin elektronik para kuruluşu olarak faaliyet gösterme iznini iptal etti. 10 Kasım tarihli karar, 11 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmî Gazete'de yayımlandı. Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası (TCMB), Ozan Elektronik Para AŞ'nin elektronik para kuruluşu olarak faaliyet gösterme iznini iptal etti. Karar, 11 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmî Gazete'de yayımlandı. Faaliyet izni iptal edildi CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle TCMB'nin 10 Kasım 2026 tarihli ve 12111/21710 sayılı kararıyla Ozan Elektronik Para AŞ'nin faaliyet izninin iptal edilmesine karar verildi. Şirkete, 6 Eylül 2019 tarihli ve 8538 sayılı Bankacılık Düzenleme ve Denetleme Kurulu kararıyla, 6493 sayılı Kanun kapsamında elektronik para kuruluşu olarak faaliyet gösterme izni verilmişti. İptal kararının dayanağı Resmî Gazete'de yayımlanan kararda, faaliyet izninin 6493 sayılı Kanun'un 16'ncı maddesinin birinci fıkrasının (c) ve (e) bentleri, 19'uncu maddesi ve 21'inci maddesinin sekizinci fıkrası uyarınca iptal edildiği belirtildi.

Lisansı iptal edildi - TCMB, A Ödeme ve Elektronik Para Hizmetleri AŞ'nin ödeme ve elektronik para kuruluşu olarak faaliyet gösterme iznini iptal etti. Karar, 11 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmî Gazete'de yayımlandı. Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası (TCMB), A Ödeme ve Elektronik Para Hizmetleri AŞ'nin faaliyet iznini iptal etti. 11 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmî Gazete'de yayımlanan kararla şirketin ödeme kuruluşu ve elektronik para kuruluşu olarak faaliyet gösterme yetkisi sona erdi. Şirkete, 27 Ekim 2022 tarihli ve 11333/20932 sayılı Banka kararıyla 6493 sayılı Ödeme ve Menkul Kıymet Mutabakat Sistemleri, Ödeme Hizmetleri ve Elektronik Para Kuruluşları Hakkında Kanun kapsamında ödeme kuruluşu ve elektronik para kuruluşu olarak faaliyet gösterme izni verilmişti. Karar Resmî Gazete'de yayımlandı İzin iptali, 6493 sayılı Kanun'un 16'ncı maddesinin birinci fıkrasının (c) bendi ile 19'uncu maddesi uyarınca gerçekleştirildi. Karar, 11 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmî Gazete'de yayımlanarak duyuruldu.

articles.articleText: Güney Kore'den ithal protez diş parçalarına damping! Kilogram başına 320 dolar uygulanacak - Ticaret Bakanlığı, Güney Kore menşeli protez diş bağlantı parçalarının ithalatında damping önlemlerini güncelledi. Bazı firmalara yüzde 15, bazılarına kilogram başına 140 veya 320 dolar, diğer firmalara ise yüzde 25 önlem uygulanacak. Ticaret Bakanlığı, Güney Kore menşeli protez dişlerin bağlantı parçalarının ithalatında uygulanan dampinge karşı önlemleri güncelledi. Yeni düzenlemeyle bazı üreticiler için yüzde 15 oranındaki önlem korunurken, bazı firmalara kilogram başına 140 ve 320 dolar tutarında önlem getirildi. Bazı üreticilere kilogram başına 320 dolar önlem CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 11 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmî Gazete'de yayımlanan tebliğle, 2025/4 sayılı İthalatta Haksız Rekabetin Önlenmesine İlişkin Tebliğ'in ilgili maddesindeki tablo değiştirildi. 9021.29.00.00.00 GTİP numaralı, protez dişlerin bağlantı parçalarını kapsayan ürünlerde Güney Kore menşeli ithalata yönelik dampinge karşı önlemler firma bazında yeniden düzenlendi. Düzenlemeye göre Dio Corporation için kilogram başına 140 dolar, Evidence Implant Inc. ve Megagen Implant Co. Ltd. için kilogram başına 320 dolar önlem uygulanacak. Diğer firmalar için yüzde 15 ve yüzde 25 oranları ACH Medical, Biotem, Cowellmedi, Dentis, Dentium, KJ Meditech, Neobiotech ve Osstem Implant şirketleri için CIF bedelinin yüzde 15'i oranında dampinge karşı önlem belirlendi. Listede yer almayan diğer firmalar için ise CIF bedelinin yüzde 25'i oranında önlem uygulanacak. Tebliğ, yayımlandığı tarihte yürürlüğe girecek ve hükümlerini Ticaret Bakanı yürütecek.

articles.summaryTr: İspanya, TikTok'ta çocuk cinsel istismarı içeren videoların 48 milyon kez izlendiğini ortaya koyan araştırmanın ardından platformdan içerikler kaldırılana kadar ülkedeki faaliyetlerini askıya almasını istedi.
articles.articleText: İspanya'dan TikTok'a sert talep: Çocuk istismarı bitene kadar faaliyetleri durdurun! - İspanya, TikTok'ta çocuk cinsel istismarı içeren videoların 48 milyon kez izlendiğini ortaya koyan araştırmanın ardından platformdan içerikler kaldırılana kadar ülkedeki faaliyetlerini askıya almasını istedi. İspanya hükümeti, TikTok'ta çocuk cinsel istismarı içeren videoların en az 48 milyon kez izlendiğini ortaya koyan araştırmanın ardından platformdan ülkedeki faaliyetlerini askıya almasını istedi. Gençlik Bakanlığı, konuyla ilgili savcılığa ve Veri Koruma Ajansı'na başvurdu. 1.183 paylaşım belgelendi CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle İspanyol doğrulama kuruluşu Maldita.es'in yayımladığı araştırmada, TikTok'ta çocuk cinsel istismarını açıkça gösteren videoların en az 48 milyon kez görüntülendiği tespit edildi. Araştırmada toplam 1.183 müstehcen paylaşım belgelendi. Ayrıca 26 binden fazla profilin söz konusu içeriklere yorum yaptığı veya bu paylaşımları yeniden dolaşıma soktuğu belirtildi. İspanya hükümeti savcılığa başvurdu Gençlik Bakanlığı'nın açıklamasına göre, TikTok'u İspanya'da tek başına yasaklama yetkisi bulunmayan Gençlik Bakanı Sira Rego, platforma karşı adım atılması için savcılığa ve Veri Koruma Ajansı'na başvurdu. Rego, konuya ilişkin açıklamasında, "Sosyal medya hukuksuz bir alan olamaz" dedi. Talep, Başbakan Pedro Sanchez hükümetinin yapay zekayla üretilen çocuk cinsel istismarı içeriklerini yaydıkları iddiasıyla X, Meta ve TikTok hakkında soruşturma açılmasını istemesinden aylar sonra geldi. TikTok bazı arama terimlerini kısıtladı Maldita.es, salı akşamı yayımladığı yeni haberde TikTok'un araştırmada çocuk istismarı içeriklerine erişim sağladığı belirlenen iki arama terimini İspanya'daki kullanıcılar için kısıtladığını bildirdi. Ancak kuruluş, diğer Avrupa ülkelerinden yapılan aramaların hâlâ aynı içeriklere ulaşılmasını sağladığını belirtti.

articles.titleTr: Fed piyasaları sarstı: ABD'de 10 yıllık tahvil faizi yeniden yüzde 5'e dayandı!
articles.summaryTr: ABD'de ekim enflasyonunun beklentileri aşması ve Fed'den gelen şahin mesajlar tahvil faizlerini yükseltti. 10 yıllık tahvil getirisi yüzde 5'e ulaşırken, aralık ayında faiz artırımı beklentileri güçlendi.
articles.articleText: Fed piyasaları sarstı: ABD'de 10 yıllık tahvil faizi yeniden yüzde 5'e dayandı! - ABD'de ekim enflasyonunun beklentileri aşması ve Fed'den gelen şahin mesajlar tahvil faizlerini yükseltti. 10 yıllık tahvil getirisi yüzde 5'e ulaşırken, aralık ayında faiz artırımı beklentileri güçlendi. ABD'de ekim ayı enflasyonunun beklentileri aşması ve Fed yetkilisi Christopher Waller'ın sert faiz artışı mesajı vermesi, tahvil piyasasında satışları hızlandırdı. 10 yıllık ABD Hazine tahvilinin getirisi yüzde 5'e yükselirken, aralık ayında faiz artırımı beklentileri güçlendi. 10 yıllık tahvil faizi yüzde 5 seviyesine çıktı CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle ABD Hazine tahvillerinde getiriler salı günü yükseldi. Gösterge niteliğindeki 10 yıllık tahvilin faizi 14 baz puan artışla yüzde 5'e ulaştı. 30 yıllık tahvilin getirisi 11 baz puandan fazla yükselerek yüzde 5,37'ye, Fed'in kısa vadeli faiz beklentilerini yakından izleyen 2 yıllık tahvilin getirisi ise 19 baz puan artışla yüzde 4,738'e çıktı. 10 yıllık tahvil faizi, bu ayın başlarında da yüzde 5 seviyesinin üzerinde işlem görmüştü. Ekim ayında 10 ve 30 yıllık tahvil getirileri 24 yılın en yüksek seviyelerine ulaşmıştı. Tahvil piyasasındaki satışları, 42 milyar dolarlık 10 yıllık tahvil ihalesine gelen görece zayıf talep de hızlandırdı. İhale sonrasında tahvil getirileri bir miktar daha yükseldi. ABD enflasyonu beklentileri aştı ABD'de tüketici fiyat endeksi (TÜFE) ekim ayında aylık yüzde 0,4 arttı. Ekonomistlerin beklentisi yüzde 0,3 seviyesindeydi. Eylül ayında aylık enflasyon yüzde 0,6 olarak açıklanmıştı. Gıda ve enerji fiyatlarının hariç tutulduğu çekirdek TÜFE ise aylık yüzde 0,3 yükseldi. Piyasa beklentisi yüzde 0,2 artış yönündeydi. Çekirdek enflasyon eylül ayında da yüzde 0,3 artmıştı. Waller'dan 50 baz puanlık faiz artışı mesajı Fed Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Christopher Waller, enflasyon verilerinin beklentilerin üzerinde gelmesi durumunda daha güçlü adımlar atılması gerektiğini söyledi. İngiltere Merkez Bankası'nın ev sahipliğinde Londra'da düzenlenen konferansta konuşan Waller, aralık ayındaki toplantıda 50 baz puanlık faiz artışının değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini belirtti. Waller, yalnızca 25 baz puanlık artışın Fed'in güvenilirliğini riske atabileceğini ifade etti. Goldman Sachs Asset Management Çok Sektörlü Sabit Getirili Yatırımlar Başkanı Lindsay Rosner da yüksek enflasyonun Fed'in faiz artırımlarını 2027'ye taşıyabileceği uyarısında bulundu. Rosner, aralık ayında faiz artırımını temel beklentileri olarak gördüklerini ve 2027'de yeni artışların da ihtimal dahilinde olduğunu söyledi. Piyasalar aralık ayında faiz artırımını fiyatlıyor CME Group'un FedWatch aracına göre piyasalar, Fed'in aralık ayında 25 baz puanlık faiz artırımını büyük ölçüde fiyatlamış durumda. Geçen cuma açıklanan ve beklentilerin iki katından fazla gelen istihdam verisi de faiz artışı beklentilerini güçlendirmişti. Petrol fiyatlarındaki gerileme ise enflasyon beklentileri açısından farklı bir görünüm oluşturdu. Brent petrolün varil fiyatı, ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'ın İran'la savaşın yakında sona erebileceğine ilişkin açıklamalarının ardından salı sabahı ağustos ayından bu yana ilk kez 90 doların altına indi. Fed'in gelecek dönemdeki faiz kararlarında cuma günü açıklanacak toptan enflasyon verileri de belirleyici olacak.

articles.articleText: Nvidia'da Jensen Huang krizi büyüyor! Şirket soruşturma için dev hukuk firması ile anlaştı - Nvidia, CEO Jensen Huang hakkındaki iddiaları araştırmak için Wachtell, Lipton & Rosen hukuk firmasını görevlendirdi. Şirket sırları ve ulusal güvenliğin tehlikeye girip girmediği incelenirken Nvidia hisseleri yüzde 6 geriledi. Nvidia Yönetim Kurulu, CEO Jensen Huang hakkındaki iddiaları incelemek üzere ABD'nin önde gelen hukuk firmalarından Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz'ı görevlendirdi. Bağımsız soruşturma kapsamında şirket sırlarının veya ulusal güvenliğin tehlikeye girip girmediği araştırılacak. Nvidia'dan bağımsız soruşturma kararı CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Nvidia Yönetim Kurulu, salı günü yaptığı açıklamada, bağımsız yönetim kurulu üyelerinin eski New York Güney Bölgesi Vekil ABD Savcısı Joon H. Kim'i ve görev yaptığı Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz hukuk firmasını kapsamlı bir soruşturma yürütmek üzere görevlendirdiğini duyurdu. Açıklamada, soruşturmanın bağımsız ve kapsamlı şekilde yürütüleceği belirtildi. Kim'in bu ayın başında hukuk firmasına katıldığı bildirildi. news.titleTr: Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair
news.summaryTr: The appointment was made after it emerged Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman believed to be a spy for China.
news.articleText: Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair - Published Nvidia has hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate the affair between its chief executive and an alleged Chinese spy. Jensen Huang, a co-founder of Nvidia who has led it to become one of the most valuable companies in the world, admitted to having a romantic relationship with a woman outside of his marriage. The woman, Alice Huang, is alleged to be a spy for Beijing. She was an executive at a Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has been a customer of Nvidia. Nvidia said on Tuesday that Wachtell attorney Joon Kim was set to lead "a thorough and independent investigation" into Jensen Huang's affair. The FBI is also conducting its own probe. Nvidia is widely considered one of the most important companies behind the US artificial intelligence (AI) boom given it is the sole manufacturer of a crucial computer chip required for successfully operating AI tools. Shares in the company fell to a near-yearly low on Tuesday, wiping more than $500bn (£375bn) off Nvidia's stock market value since Friday, even as tech stocks have recovered since last week's sell-off. Jensen Huang's relationship with an executive of an Nvidia customer, who is also believed by the US government to be spying for China, has business and national security implications. Megaspeed had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia has said was investigated and debunked. Nvidia has also maintained the US government did not inform the firm that Megaspeed posed an intelligence concern. According to the New York Times, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington in spring of this year warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy. Beijing has rejected claims that Jensen Huang has been targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "intended to smear and malign China". US President Donald Trump said Monday that he had spoken to Jensen Huang and that the Nvidia boss told him "I had no idea she was a spy." Trump said he believed the him. However, the relationship has drawn more political attention. Congressional leaders of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs have asked Jensen Huang to appear next week for a closed door briefing. The Nvidia boss has yet to say whether he will attend, a person familiar with the committee's demand told the BBC. The committee has the authority to subpoena Jensen Huang, effectively forcing him to appear before the committee, if deemed necessary. When announcing on Sunday that it would investigate the affair, Nvidia's board said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised. It added that a committee of independent directors would oversee the probe. - What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy - Published40 minutes ago Joon Kim, who will lead Nvidia's investigation, is a former US Attorney for New York's Southern District and spent several years working as a government attorney focused on fraud and other criminal acts. Wachtell is one of the largest law firms in the US and has several notable clients in the tech industry. Among them are OpenAI and Salesforce. The investigation will likely be treated as urgent, according to sources familiar with the matter, as Jensen Huang's public image is tightly intertwined with Nvidia. news.titleTr: Can crypto trust firms compete with banks in US derivatives settlements?
news.summaryTr: Crypto custodians are moving into a market handling billions in daily settlements, but regulatory relief and a shift in congressional control leave questions over their long-term role.
news.articleText: Can crypto trust firms compete with banks in US derivatives settlements? Crypto custodians are moving into a market handling billions in daily settlements, but regulatory relief and a shift in congressional control leave questions over their long-term role. Crypto companies are moving deeper into financial services traditionally dominated by banks, seeking a role in US derivatives settlements, where billions of dollars change hands daily. The push comes as regulators expand the services trust companies can provide, even as traditional banking groups challenge parts of the regulatory framework governing crypto firms’ expansion into banklike activities. A Nov. 5 decision by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) illustrates the shift, allowing derivatives clearinghouses to use trust companies for daily settlements with clearing members, a function previously restricted to banks under the agency’s regulations. The relief could create new business opportunities for regulated crypto custodians, but its revocable nature and changes in the US political landscape raise questions about the durability of the regulatory opening. Crypto firms eye billions in daily derivatives settlements The scale of the derivatives settlement business offers some perspective on the opportunity. CME Group, one of the world’s largest derivatives market operators, transferred an average of $8.7 billion per business day through its clearing systems during the first half of 2026, up from $6.7 billion a day in 2025, according to regulatory filings. Those figures represent funds transferred between clearing firms to settle gains and losses, rather than fees earned by settlement banks. They nevertheless illustrate the scale of financial flows supported by the infrastructure that trust companies could increasingly help provide. The CFTC’s Division of Clearing and Risk issued no-action relief on Nov. 5 following an Oct. 29 request from derivatives clearinghouse Nodal Clear, allowing clearinghouses to use trust companies for daily settlements if they meet the same evaluation and monitoring requirements applied to traditional settlement banks. The decision addresses an inconsistency between federal commodities law, which permits customer funds to be held at banks or trust companies, and CFTC Regulation 39.14, which defines settlement banks only as banks. Nodal Clear partnered with Coinbase in 2025 to integrate USDC into US futures trading. Coinbase Custody Trust was already expected to provide daily settlement services under the arrangement, Cointelegraph has learned. Related: CFTC expands regulatory relief for passive trading software providers Other crypto firms have also expanded their institutional financial services. On Nov. 4, BitGo launched its Global Markets division, combining derivatives trading, financing, collateral management and settlement capabilities. Coinbase’s national trust bank charter also took effect on Nov. 6, allowing Coinbase National Trust Company, a separate entity from Coinbase Custody Trust, to provide federally supervised digital asset custody services. Several major crypto firms have also secured US national trust bank approvals over the past months, including Circle, Ripple, Crypto.com and Stripe-owned Bridge. The charters, granted by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), reflect the industry’s expansion into federally regulated financial services. Traditional banks contest crypto firms’ expanding role The expansion of specialized trust companies has prompted objections from traditional banking groups. In October, the Independent Community Bankers of America sued the OCC, arguing that its national trust bank charter rules could allow crypto firms to conduct certain banklike activities without meeting all the requirements imposed on conventional banks. The lawsuit reflects a broader disagreement over how specialized financial institutions should be regulated as they expand into services also provided by banks. Cody Carbone, CEO of The Digital Chamber, told Cointelegraph that the CFTC’s relief does not put trust companies in a better or worse position than traditional banks. Trust companies and banks already compete for services permitted under their respective charters, Carbone said, adding that the decision gives clearinghouses more options without preventing banks from retaining their business. “A trust company charter is not a regulatory shortcut,” he said. Revocable relief faces a changing regulatory landscape Despite the potential opportunities, the CFTC’s decision leaves questions about how securely trust companies can establish a long-term role in derivatives settlement. The agency issued a no-action letter rather than formally amending its regulations. The letter states that CFTC staff will not recommend enforcement action against clearinghouses using trust companies for daily settlements if specified conditions are met. Unlike a formal rule amendment, which generally requires a public notice-and-comment process, staff no-action relief does not change the underlying regulation and can be withdrawn. “A change in Commission leadership could withdraw the CFTC Letter. More formal Commission action, such as amending the regulation, would be necessary to avoid this potential risk,” Jordan Yeagley, a shareholder at Buchanan Ingersoll & Rooney, told Cointelegraph. The uncertainty comes at a politically significant moment for the agency. CFTC Chair Michael Selig remains the regulator’s sole commissioner, despite a statutory structure providing for five commissioners. Selig has led the agency since December 2025, leaving four seats vacant as the regulator expands its work on digital asset markets. The political environment is also changing following the Nov. 3 US midterm elections, in which Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress. The incoming Congress, which takes office in January, will have greater power to scrutinize the CFTC’s regulatory agenda. The Senate also has a role in confirming nominees to fill the agency’s vacant commissioner seats, while the House and Senate Agriculture Committees oversee the regulator. Sen. Sherrod Brown, who won Ohio’s Senate race on Nov. 3 despite more than $60 million in opposition spending from crypto-backed political action committees, could take on a prominent role on the Senate Agriculture Committee.
